flows.title: Choose a plan
flows.task: The customer is deciding between two plans and wants to know what changes.
flows.hypothesis: Putting the two plans side by side makes the difference legible without opening a comparison table.

entry.why: Someone weighing up plans arrives on the marketing site before they ever see pricing.

review.proposal: People reach pricing from the marketing navigation.
review.question: Do people arrive on pricing from the site, or from an ad landing straight on it?

review.proposal: One click from the marketing navigation to pricing.
review.question: Is pricing findable from every marketing page, or only the home page?

review.proposal: Pick a plan, or leave without picking one.
review.question: Is there a third path — talk to sales, or start a trial without choosing?

review.proposal: Nothing is submitted on these screens, so there is no failure to show.
After choosing, pricing shows the selected plan.
review.question: The destination after selecting a plan was never observed. Is this what it does?

flows.title: Answer a billing question
flows.task: The customer has a question about proration before committing.

entry.why: The billing questions sit on the pricing page itself, below the plan cards.

review.proposal: The questions are on the pricing page, below the plans.
No navigation: the answer expands in place.
One question, one answer. No branch.
Expanding an answer cannot fail in a way worth showing.
The answer stays open and the plans stay visible below it.
